subject: Urgent: High latency & error spike on inference endpoints — suspected peering/DNS/proxy path
participants_external: rajiv.patel@acme-analytics.com (Rajiv Patel, Network Lead, Acme Analytics)
content:
From: David Morgan <david.morgan@acme-analytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Cc: ops+infra@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent - severe latency & errors on inference endpoints

Marissa / Sean,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx rates and tail latency for the /v1/generate endpoints around 08:50 UTC. Error rate is ~14% for a representative set of requests and p95 latency has jumped from ~300ms to >2.5s. This is impacting customer-facing features across our product lines.

Attached sample logs and a tcpdump capture from one of our NAT instances. From our side we see repeated TCP retransmits toward Redwood's peering IPs and many SYN+RST cycles. We are currently routing through our outbound proxy and have had no config changes in the last 48h.

We need immediate assistance to identify whether this is a Redwood routing/peering problem, a DNS resolution issue, or something on our side (proxy/firewall). Please escalate to engineering and execs as required; our leadership is standing by.

- David
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example

Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: URGENT Escalation — Acme Analytics latency/errors (possible peering/DNS/proxy)

Team,

Acme (DEAL-57321) reporting 14% 5xx, p95 latency >2.5s beginning ~08:50 UTC. External tcpdump shows TCP retransmits toward our peering addresses and proxy timeouts. They are routing through an outbound proxy/NAT.

What to check (priority):
- Peering/VPN session counters (peer flaps, packet drops) for their account's dedicated peer (peer-id: acme-peer-us-west-2).
- BGP update churn and AS paths for the affected prefixes.
- DNS resolution paths: is acme resolving to a Redwood CDN/edge IP or our regional public IP? Check our authoritative DNS timing and recent changes.
- Firewall/proxy: inspect our edge proxies for 502/504 surge and connection resets. Look for long queue times and backend backend_conn errors.
- KV/cache saturation and GPU queueing metrics for the served model (may explain p95).

Attachments: I've included their logs (redwood_request_logs_0417.zip) and their tcpdump summary (tcpdump_acme_peer_0417.txt) from their initial mail.

Business impact: multiple enterprise customers affected; Acme's CxO is involved. Please prioritize. If this is a peering-related route flap or a DNS/TTL regression, we should consider an immediate fallback routing to an alternate region or a temporary capacity shift for Acme's dedicated segment.

Asking for a 30-minute triage update and an exec note for Laura to send if we need to offer credits or an SLA exception.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@acme-analytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Cc: ops+infra@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:59:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent - severe latency & errors on inference endpoints

Marissa,

Quick update from our network team (summary of tcpdump attached):
- We see SYN retries and TLS handshake timeouts between our NAT gateway (10.18.4.12) and a /32 address that resolves to redwood-edge-us-west-2.redwood.example.com.
- Packet captures show consistent RSTs that coincide with proxy keepalive timeouts; some flows are being reset by our outbound proxy during slow responses.
- No recent changes on our side; proxy config is stable.
- We also observed varying DNS answers for the edge hostname, TTLs appear short (~30s) and occasionally return a different regional IP (~us-east-1) which then times out.

We can try two quick workarounds while you triage:
1) Bypass the outbound proxy for calls to redwood-edge-us-west-2.redwood.example.com (whitelist the host) — low-risk and quick.
2) Add a direct route for the /32 to go via a secondary NAT (bypass the proxy path entirely).

We'll stand by to implement either if you confirm. We're also happy to provide more packet captures.

-Rajiv
Network Lead, Acme Analytics

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.example
To: david.morgan@acme-analytics.com, rajiv.patel@acme-analytics.com

Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent - severe latency & errors on inference endpoints

David/Rajiv — thanks for the details and the captures. Quick technical summary from Redwood:
- We are seeing intermittent packet drops on the peering link counters tied to acme-peer-us-west-2; there are flaps at the tunnel level between 08:48–09:03 UTC.
- Our edge proxies show a small surge of 502/504 errors correlated with backend connection queueing; GPU queue length briefly exceeded threshold in one podset during the window.
- DNS logs: we did deploy a regional traffic-shaping rule yesterday that slightly changed edge DNS priority for canary routing; TTLs should still be 60s but we are investigating a regression that could surface inconsistent answers to resolvers with short cache windows.

Immediate mitigation plan (agreed action):
- Acme to attempt proxy bypass for the edge hostname (Rajiv) — please confirm once done.
- Redwood to temporarily pin Acme's routing to the alternate regional ingress (us-east-1) for canary traffic, and to increase the edge proxy keepalive timeout for their peer.
- We'll monitor error-rate and p95 for the next 2 hours. If metrics do not improve, we'll enact full failover to the alternate region for Acme's dedicated segment.

Exec note: Laura — if we need to authorize credits or SLA exceptions, please confirm authorization level for this account.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: david.morgan@acme-analytics.com, rajiv.patel@acme-analytics.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, sean_gallagher@redwood.example, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: SUMMARY & next steps — Acme incident (latency/errors)

David / Rajiv — thank you for working through this with us. Final summary of what happened and next steps: 

Findings:
- Root cause was a combination of short-lived peering tunnel flaps (BGP session resets) and a regression in our DNS traffic-shaping canary that caused inconsistent regional answers to resolvers with short TTLs. Those two issues together increased the probability that requests would land on a slow path and be reset by Acme's outbound proxy, producing higher 5xxs and tail latency.

Actions taken:
- We rolled a fix to the DNS canary logic (reverted the priority change) and validated stable answers for the edge hostname; TTLs are back to 60s.
- We pinned Acme's traffic to the alternate ingress (us-east-1) for canary requests and increased proxy keepalive on our edge by 30s.
- Acme implemented a temporary proxy bypass for redwood-edge-us-west-2.redwood.example.com to avoid the slow proxy path while peering counters stabilize.
- We continue to monitor peering session stability; our network team will work directly with routing to identify root of flaps (scheduled deep-dive Monday).

Impact & follow-ups:
- Error-rate fell from ~14% to ~1.2% within 20 minutes of the mitigations. p95 returned to ~320ms.
- Laura: proposing to offer a goodwill credit (1 month pro-rata) and an incident RCA to their ops/execs. Please advise if you approve.
- Follow-up items: full RCA write-up (by Tue), joint packet capture comparison, and an action on hardening DNS canary gate tests.

Attachments: includes the captures and our temporary routing playbook for Acme's dedicated segment.

If you'd like an exec-level call to brief your leadership, we're available tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks again for patience — we'll keep monitoring closely.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123
